finding.name: Selection Sets and Default Treatment
finding.description: Include and exclude sets over source elements, the default treatment applied to everything the sets do not name, and whether the shape is closed against elements it has never seen.

questions.text: What treatment applies to a source element that neither the include nor the exclude set names?
answer_data: default treatment code (omit, deny, mask, pass-through)
justification for a default other than omit

questions.text: When an include path and an exclude path both match one element, which prevails and on what rule?
Which elements must survive selection for the output to remain usable, and what happens when the policy would remove them?
answer_data: failure mode code (refuse, serve degraded, empty result)

questions.text: How is an element treated that was added to the source after this shape was authored?

data_elements.name: Include path set
data_elements.description: Ordered set of path expressions naming elements permitted to leave.

data_elements.name: Exclude path set
data_elements.description: Ordered set of path expressions naming elements that must not leave.

data_elements.name: Default treatment
data_elements.description: Code applied to any element not matched by either set; default-deny is the expected value.

data_elements.name: Closure mode
data_elements.description: Whether the shape is closed (unknown elements never leave) or open (unknown elements follow the default).

finding.inline_only_rationale: Selection sets and their default are the policy record's own declarative content: structured values held with the policy, not a separate deliverable. Any file, table or document form is a projection of those values, so declaring an artifact here would confuse the shape with one of its encodings.

finding.name: Expansion, include, and hierarchical node selection
finding.description: Output shape is a graph, not only a column list. OData $expand includes related resources inline and may nest $select; context URLs describe projected+expanded entities. GraphQL selection sets are hierarchical down to scalars. FHIR _include/_revinclude add referenced resources; they cannot mix with _summary=text. JSON:API compound documents require full linkage except where sparse fieldsets exclude relationship fields. XACML Multiple Decision Profile interprets a multiple:content-selector XPath as one decision per node. This model records maximum expand depth, allowed navigation paths, and whether related resources inherit the parent policy or a nested policy.

questions.text: Which navigation/relationship paths may be expanded, and to what maximum depth?
Does each expanded type use this policy, a nested projection-policy reference, or inherit parent treatments?
For hierarchical XML/JSON resources, is a content-selector (XPath/JSONPath) used to name the nodes whose shape is governed, analogous to XACML multiple:content-selector?

data_elements.name: allowed_navigation_paths
data_elements.description: Navigation or relationship paths that may be expanded inline.

data_elements.name: max_expand_depth
data_elements.description: Maximum depth to which related resources may be expanded.

data_elements.name: nested_policy_ref
data_elements.description: Projection policy reference governing an expanded type or path.

data_elements.name: related_inherits_parent
data_elements.description: Whether expanded related resources inherit the parent policy's treatments.

data_elements.name: hierarchical_selector
data_elements.description: Content-selector language and expression naming the nodes whose shape is governed, analogous to the XACML multiple:content-selector.

artifacts.name: Field scope document
artifacts.description: Include/exclude path lists, default treatment, expansion extent, hierarchical selector, nested policy refs — compiled against one source schema version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI when published, otherwise a Dimension-assigned UUID/ULID; scoped to one policy version and one source-schema version.

finding.name: Source Schema Binding and Drift
finding.description: The dependency of a shape on a governed source schema version, how unresolved paths and newly appearing elements are detected, and who remediates.

questions.text: To which source schema or data contract version is this shape bound, and how strictly?
Which selection paths currently fail to resolve against the bound schema version?
What happens when the source adds an element this shape has never classified?
How is drift detected, how often is the check run, and when was it last run?

data_elements.name: Bound source schema reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governed source schema or data contract in WM-DAT-004.

data_elements.name: Binding strictness
data_elements.description: Whether the shape is pinned to one schema version, accepts a range, or floats.

data_elements.name: Unresolved path
data_elements.description: A declared path that no longer resolves against the bound schema version.

data_elements.name: Drift observation timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the drift check was performed, recorded separately from the schema change time.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Only the binding and its current resolution state are local; the schema itself and its validation contract are owned by WM-DAT-004. A local artifact would either copy that schema or become a second, competing source of truth about it.

finding.name: Residual Disclosure and Side Channels
finding.description: What a recipient can still infer from a served output beyond its values: existence of a response, record counts, ordering, structural shape and the difference between error, refusal and empty result.

questions.text: Which facts does a non-empty response reveal even when every value in it is masked?
Does the count, ordering or structural padding of a response leak an attribute?
Do error, refusal and empty-result responses differ in a way that discloses the withheld value?
Which of these residual channels are accepted as tolerable, and on whose authority?

data_elements.name: Residual disclosure channel
data_elements.description: An inference path that survives the declared shape, such as existence, count, order or timing.

data_elements.name: Response uniformity rule
data_elements.description: Rule making refusals, errors and empty results indistinguishable to a recipient.

data_elements.name: Padding or decoy rule
data_elements.description: Rule obscuring the true number of withheld elements or records, such as decoy digests.

data_elements.name: Accepted residual risk statement
data_elements.description: Recorded acceptance of a named residual channel, with the reference to the accepting authority.

finding.inline_only_rationale: This is analytical content attached to the policy record. The runtime behaviour that realises uniform responses and padding is executed by WM-XCT-038, so declaring an artifact here would imply this model produces or holds the responses themselves.

finding.name: Binding Target, Audience and Effective Window
finding.description: The attachment of one shape to a contract or grant, object type or audience class, with the window in which it is effective and the authority the binding presupposes.

questions.text: What is the target of this binding, and which model owns that target?
answer_data: target kind code (contract, grant, object type, audience)

questions.text: Which recipient class does the binding serve, and how is that class defined without copying party records?
From when until when is the binding effective, and what governs an output already served under it?
Which authority must exist for this binding to be publishable at all, and what happens if it is absent?

data_elements.name: Binding identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the attachment record linking one shape to one target.

data_elements.name: Binding target reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the contract, grant, object type or audience the shape is attached to.

data_elements.name: Effective from
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant from which the binding applies.

data_elements.name: Effective until
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant after which the binding no longer applies; absent means open-ended.

finding.inline_only_rationale: A binding is a link record composed almost entirely of references. Materialising it would duplicate contract and party content owned by WM-XCT-002 and WM-XCT-001 and create a second place where an authorization appears to be recorded.

finding.name: Class-to-Treatment Minimum Matrix
finding.description: The governed table mapping an externally assigned sensitivity class to the weakest treatment a shape may apply, so that shapes can be checked mechanically rather than by reviewer opinion.

questions.text: For each referenced sensitivity class, what is the weakest treatment a shape may apply?
Which classification scheme and version does the matrix key on, and how are keys resolved?
How is a shape checked against the matrix, and what constitutes a violation?
What happens to existing shapes when an element is reclassified upward?
answer_data: required outcome code (recompile, withdraw, withhold element)

data_elements.name: Sensitivity class key
data_elements.description: Externally assigned class identifier that the matrix row is keyed on.

data_elements.name: Minimum treatment
data_elements.description: Weakest treatment code permitted for elements carrying the class.

data_elements.name: Classification scheme version
data_elements.description: Version of the external scheme the matrix is valid against.

artifacts.name: Sensitivity Class Treatment Matrix
artifacts.description: A reusable governed decision table binding each externally assigned sensitivity class to the minimum treatment any shape must apply, maintained independently of any single policy and cited by every shape it constrains.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier of the matrix in the adopting Dimension's policy register, qualified by the referenced classification scheme identifier and version; a governed IRI where the register issues one, otherwise a Dimension-assigned ULID. A content digest verifies integrity only; no date forms part of the identity.

finding.name: Release-Set Linkability
finding.description: The widening of disclosure when several shapes are served over the same population to the same or colluding recipients, through shared join keys, repeated queries or overlapping grains.

questions.text: Which other shapes may be served over the same subjects to the same recipient class?
Which elements act as join keys across shapes, and how is that overlap controlled?
How many times may this shape be served over one population before the combined disclosure exceeds the claim?
How is a change in the surrounding release set detected after this shape was approved?

data_elements.name: Companion shape reference
data_elements.description: Another shape servable over the same population to the same recipient class.

data_elements.name: Join key element
data_elements.description: Element whose values allow records from two shapes to be linked.

data_elements.name: Release budget reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the composition budget or release counter owned by WM-XCT-005.

data_elements.name: Declared release limit
data_elements.description: Maximum number of releases of this shape over one population before re-review.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Linkability is a declared property of a set of shapes. Counting actual releases, maintaining a budget and enforcing a limit are runtime activities owned by WM-XCT-005 and WM-XCT-038, so no local artifact may hold a running total.

finding.name: Shape Invalidation Signals
finding.description: The observable conditions that make a shape unfit - upward reclassification, schema drift, changed adversary context, expired assurance, regime change - recorded as signals with safe interim behaviour and an explicit hand-off, not as a state machine.

questions.text: Which observable signals indicate that this shape may now under-protect?
What is the safe interim behaviour between detecting a signal and resolving it?
answer_data: interim behaviour code (withhold element, serve narrower shape, refuse)

questions.text: Which model executes the resulting withdrawal or supersession, and what is handed to it?
How is a long absence of signals distinguished from a shape nobody is monitoring?

data_elements.name: Invalidation signal
data_elements.description: A detected condition suggesting the shape no longer protects adequately, with its originating model.

data_elements.name: Interim behaviour
data_elements.description: The conservative behaviour declared for the period between detection and resolution.

data_elements.name: Signal observation timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the signal was observed here, recorded separately from the instant the underlying change occurred.

data_elements.name: Monitoring coverage statement
data_elements.description: Which signals are actively monitored for this shape and which are not.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Signals and interim behaviour are declarative annotations on the shape. State transitions, approval and supersession are executed by WM-KNW-012 and any runtime response by WM-XCT-038, so an artifact here would be mistaken for a lifecycle record this model does not own.
